entries.statement: A manga's Wikipedia-sourced volume_boundaries rows (source 'wikipedia', grouped by manga_anilist_id|source_page) come from a page whose title-token overlap with EVERY title/title_english/synonym of the series on that manga is below 0.5.

Disposition: reported only (no auto-fix, no flag). Threshold 0.5 and the STOP-word list (line 540) are constants embedded in the class with no named rule.

entries.statement: For a manga where at least one series row has manga_status 'finished' and a known total_chapters, any Wikipedia boundary row whose chapter_start exceeds the max total_chapters across those series.
entries.notes: Second half of §10 'Volume-boundary identity + numbering space' — comment: 'for a finished manga with a known total, must not run past the total (shared pages list sequels)'. entries.statement: Within one manga's Wikipedia boundary set ordered by volume: (a) a row whose chapter_end is below its chapter_start, or (b) a row whose chapter_start does not exceed the previous volume's chapter_start.
bundle_parts: a boundary's end precedes its start
a boundary's start does not exceed the previous volume's start

Disposition: reported with instruction 'run heal-volume-boundaries.ts' — not auto-fixed here. Rationale in comment: each impossible row silently mis-labels the volume of every chapter after it.

entries.statement: A series' maximum episode number exceeds max(total_episodes, max component episode_end, aired_episodes) — episodes outrun the component structure.

entries.statement: Against the DISPLAY total (same-edition band: latest_known_chapters when it lies in [0.8×total_chapters, total_chapters), else total_chapters): (a) an anchor chapter above it, (b) a start_chapter above it, or (c) a continue_chapter above it + 1 — a count-space value in a number-space instrument.

anchor.start_chapter > display total (START lives strictly inside the run)
anchor.continue_chapter > display total + 1 (CONTINUE may sit exactly one past: post_series = coverage+1)

entries.statement: An anchor whose chapter is non-integer and whose source is neither 'manual' nor 'wiki' — a derived fractional anchor is a bonus/Memoire chapter mis-scraped from a source chart.

aired_episodes and total_episodes never exceed the community cap

entries.statement: Per series: (a) zero episode rows while aired_episodes > 0 (ALL eps title_pending, canon-tier); or (b) one or more rows with null/blank title; or (c) fewer rows than aired_episodes (AFL lag — the missing eps render title_pending).

some episode rows have empty titles
episode row count < aired_episodes

entries.statement: Episodes carrying a rearranged or graft annotation are settled reorders: monotonicity and start-trend checks skip them (either the episode or its predecessor).

entries.statement: Beyond the mapped frontier, a null chapter is the honest state and is never a failure; inside the frontier, a null on a canon/mixed row is a failure unless the row sits in a reorder crossing.

entries.statement: Stale non-MU anchors with no MU frontier must render their truthful-but-old 'as of ep N'; synthesis must NOT override them (a diverged anime would claim full coverage) — research closes them, never a guess.
entries.notes: Enforced by branch ORDER in the audit (maxAnchor !== undefined checked before the finished+total_chapters synthesis branch); whether the display side enforces the same order is not stated here.

entries.statement: MU chapter numbering diverging more than 20% from AniList's count means different editions (or release-derived garbage on an old manga): latest_known_chapters is null-healed and a 'count_mismatch' flag asks which is the reading edition.
entries.notes: The 20% figure appears only in the flag note text; the band itself lives in the lib (lib home should carry the constant). AUTO-HEAL: latest_known_chapters is rewritten every run for every MU-linked manga (line 93-96).

entries.statement: AFG identity resolution proceeds by tiers — registry, then RULED, then slug equality (our id / afl_slug / slugified title), then whitespace-insensitive FULL title/synonym equality, then subtitle-stripped prefix equality (≥5 chars) — and a key claimed by two series is ambiguous and never auto-matches unless the episode span (±2 of our max or a component boundary) independently singles one out; prefix matches register ONLY with span agreement.
bundle_parts: registry match (series_external_ids source 'afg') wins outright
RULED map overrides all automatic tiers; null = ruled NOT a match
slug tier: AFG slug or slugified AFG title equals our id / afl_slug / slugified title
title tier: squashed full title equals any of our title / title_english / synonyms
prefix tier: colon/dash/paren-cut prefix of ≥5 chars equals one of our names — registers only when span agrees
ambiguity (>1 candidate) at any tier resolves by span agreement or is reported for ruling, never auto-matched
span agreement = within ±2 of our episode max (episodes table, else aired_episodes) or of any component episode_end
entries.notes: Comment: 'two weak signals must agree'; 'identity-first, flag-first'. The tier logic is inlined in this script, not in lib (the daily AFG refresh 'cross-checks them from then on' via the registry, per header).

entries.statement: One afg id per series (registry constraint): when several pages match one series the strongest tier is registered and the rest reported; an existing registration is never overwritten; registration dismisses the page's open 'match_ambiguous' flags.
bundle_parts: one afg id per series
never overwrite an existing afg registration
registering closes open match_ambiguous flags for that slug
entries.notes: Whether the registry table itself enforces uniqueness is not stated in this file.

entries.statement: AFG sparse pages: a page whose episode table stops far short of the run (or has <6 episodes) is a stale or absent structural signal, not evidence of the series' extent.
